grand_strategy.reading:
North Korea is Luttwak's small adversary that became useful to a great power and
sold its usefulness dear. For thirty years its strategy was survival by
nuisance: weapons as the one asset a poor, sanctioned state could produce. The
war in Ukraine gave that asset a buyer. Since the treaty of June 2024 Kim has
turned shells, missiles, labour and an expeditionary force into cash, fuel,
food and technology, escaped the diplomatic quarantine, and made both Moscow
and Beijing court him. He has also removed the questions that used to bind
him: the UN panel is gone, denuclearisation is struck from every agenda,
reunification is struck from the constitution, and the Party Congress of
February 2026 wrote the status into policy. Pyongyang no longer asks to be
admitted to the order; it asks that the arsenal be accepted as a fact. The
paradoxes are all of one kind. Each success rests on a patron's need, not on
a strength of Pyongyang's own: the Russian income ends with the war, the
Chinese trade ends when Beijing chooses, the nuclear status leaves nothing to
bargain with, and the sanctions workaround turns the cyber and labour
earners into the targets of a coalition that no veto can dissolve. Two
signals that are not rows: the Ninth Congress's work report did not mention
Russia or China, and Kim has not met a US president since 2019 while Trump
keeps saying he will. The open question for 2027 is whether the same hand can
manage the end of the Russian war, a Trump offer that asks for the arsenal,
and a thirteen-year-old heir.

stances.note: Treaty ally. The Comprehensive Strategic Partnership Treaty signed in Pyongyang on 19 Jun 2024 (ratified in Moscow on 6 Nov 2024) obliges each side to military assistance if the other is attacked; Pyongyang used it by sending the Kursk force (confirmed by Moscow on 26 Apr 2025 and by Pyongyang on 28 Apr), a missile unit and about 12 million shells, and receives cash, oil above the UN cap, food and technology (USD 10-14bn on Bloomberg's count). Kim and Putin met again in Beijing on 3 Sep 2025 and the first road bridge opened in Sep 2026. Sources mirrored from Russia's card (same links). Friction is thin: the Ninth Congress report did not mention Russia, and the terms are Moscow's to end with the war, which is why this is a paradox and not a plain gain. Bond - affinity: Soviet-era patronage renewed, not kinship.

stances.note: Rival, not adversary - argued. For: Kim calls South Korea the 'most hostile' state and 'principal enemy', threatens to 'completely destroy' it if threatened, has cut roads and rails, fortified the line since 2024 and has made the doctrine constitutional. Against: the ontology reserves 'adversary' for a declared aim of the other's defeat or disappearance, and the doctrine of December 2023 says the opposite - Pyongyang gave up absorbing the South, wrote reunification out of the constitution (March 2026), defines the South as a bordering state and seeks separation, the destruction threat being conditional on attack. A state that fences itself off and denies the other state's claim to kinship is a rival with an arms race, not a mortal enemy; Seoul's own 'peaceful two-state' white paper (May 2026) treats it the same way. Cooling because the 2025-26 steps (Party Congress, border works, mines of 21 Sep 2026, rejection of every Seoul overture by Kim Yo Jong and the SPA speech) hardened the separation, not because of any thaw. Bond - kin: language, history and the 1948 founding claim; Pyongyang formally repudiates it, so the pair is a feud in Luttwak's sense and Pyongyang's repudiation is the bet, not yet the fact. The USA-PRK pair below is the real test of adversary and stays rival too.
